content: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to either avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, consider reducing the cannabidiol dose and monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor plasma levels closely. Conversely, carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the cariprazine dose as per the drug monograph and monitor closely. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of indinavir or other CYP3A4 substrates as needed and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ceritinib also increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity. Consider using alternative drugs or lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of inhaled ciclesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase the risk of toxicity, including Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but decreases its levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Indinavir also increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity. Consider using alternative drugs or lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor closely. Indinavir decreases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which reduces clopidogrel bioactivation. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity. Consider using alternative drugs or lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor closely. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, especially when coadministered with atazanavir, due to the risk of indirect (unconjugated) hyperbilirubinemia. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to a significant increase in cobimetinib levels. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Conivaptan also increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Crizotinib also increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. This interaction is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cyclophosphamide also increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Danazol increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darifenacin increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of darolutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely for adverse reactions and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. Dasatinib increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir also increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of desvenlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity. Consider using alternative drugs or lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of diazoxide by mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Reports of hyperglycemia have been noted with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Didanosine decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer indinavir one hour prior to didanosine chewable tablets or powder. No significant interactions have been reported with didanosine capsules. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitor for potential adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated.
